Subject: Privdeploy egress capping & NIC striping runlevel for private GPU pool

Hi Anita / Cumulus ops team —

Thanks again for the time last week. As we edge toward a scoped PoC, we want to confirm the network and capacity assumptions that will drive sizing for the privately-hosted GPU pool (VPC colocation). Attached: throughput-model_v1.xlsx (baseline numbers & simple run-rate).

Topline asks from our side so we can finalize the PoC design:
- Confirm the cross‑connect capacity (do you want a single 100Gb LAG or 2x100Gb LAGs for striping/HA?).
- Any explicit egress caps or corporate egress policies we need to honor (per-tenant or aggregate)?
- Switch oversubscription ratio in the target rack; MTU and whether jumbo frames are enabled end‑to‑end.
- Preferred vendor for colo crossconnect (Equinox / Cumulus DC / other) — we can drive ordering once you confirm.

Our throughput target for the PoC is: sustained 350 requests/sec at an average payload of ~600 tokens (estimate) with burst headroom to 1200 rps for short periods. That maps to ~210k tokens/sec sustained, with bursts up to ~720k tokens/sec. We assume NVLINK-local model shards and a single‑GPU warm pool per node for the PoC.

Initial proposal (high level):
- NIC strategy: 2x100Gb LAG per host (bonded), flow-hashed into multiple queues; stripe inference traffic across NICs at socket level.
- Egress policy: configurable policer at top-of-rack to cap tenant egress to an agreed limit with token-aware admission at the runtime layer.
- Admission control: soft-limit at 85% sustained, hard-limit at 110% burst to protect other tenants.

Can you confirm the crossconnect and egress constraints, and upload any network diagrams you have (we'll review and propose an optimized striping plan)? I copied Karthik and Laura for capacity/calculation input and procurement.

Thanks —

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick data points from our side:
- Current colo handoff supports either a single 100Gb crossconnect or dual 100Gb LAGs; we have fiber fibers already provisioned for dual 100Gb if you want HA/striping.
- Egress policy: corporate netops prefers an aggregate cap by tenant; we typically err toward a 20Gbps soft cap per tenant for production traffic unless explicitly agreed otherwise. Bursts above that are allowed with explicit guardrails.
- Rack topology: top-of-rack switches are 2:1 oversubscribed at the spine; MTU is 9216 end-to-end for current tenants.
- Vendor: Equinox Data can do same-day crossconnects for our colo; contact netops@equinox.com if you need an order.

Attaching network-diagram_v1.png showing the rack and crossconnect ports.

Given your burst numbers, we should size the LAGs to allow NIC-level striping but plan for an egress policer at the rack to limit production tenants to 20Gbps unless we contract for a higher SLA.

Best —

Anita / team —

Thanks for the diagram and the constraints. I ran the numbers against Marissa's PoC target and sketched a resilience/runlevel approach. Summary below; details and math are in the attached throughput-model_v2.xlsx.

Short summary / recommendations:
1) LAG and striping
   - Use dual 100Gb LAG per host for PoC with symmetric hashing. This gives 200Gb aggregate per host and allows us to stripe flows across NICs while preserving affinity for KV-cache hot paths.
   - Configure per‑flow hashing on the ToR and host bond mode that preserves L4 5‑tuple hashing (to avoid split of single request's TCP flow).

2) Egress capping and burst handling
   - Implement a top-of-rack policer that enforces a configurable soft cap (20Gbps default per tenant) with a token-bucket allowing short bursts up to 60Gbps for up to 12s. This matches your corporate policy but gives the runtime headroom for model burstiness.
   - On host, use tc + fq_codel shaping for fairness; runtime will do admission control when observed egress approaches the soft cap.

3) Runlevels (graceful degradation modes)
   - Runlevel 0: normal — admission at target sustained (350 rps).
   - Runlevel 1: elevated load — enable smaller model variant or 8-bit quantized replica; restrict long-context requests and reduce per-request max tokens.
   - Runlevel 2: critical — shed best-effort requests, enforce strict per-tenant token limits, route overflow to a lower-cost model in a different region (if allowed).

4) Headroom math (simple):
   - PoC sustained tokens/sec = 350 rps * 600 tokens = 210k tokens/s.
   - Burst headroom = 1200 rps * 600 = 720k tokens/s (short window).
   - With dual 100Gb LAG (200Gb aggregate) and assuming ~1.2 bytes/token on average network payload, we get ~240Gbps capacity (after overhead) which covers sustained and short bursts. The limiting factor will be the rack egress policer if set to 20Gbps per tenant — so we will need to negotiate an elevated cap for the production SLA if production traffic won't be shaped to lower-cost models during bursts.

Operational asks for PoC:
- Please confirm whether Cumulus will accept the token-bucket burst profile (60Gbps / 12s) on the rack policer.
- Confirm whether Equinox ordering is acceptable; if yes, I'll share a crossconnect form and we can schedule.
- We'll run a 48‑hour soak test during the PoC to validate runlevel transitions.

I'll attach the updated spreadsheet with per-node QPS-to-bitrate curves and recommended NIC tuning knobs.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: throughput-model_v2.xlsx

This all looks good. Quick answers and next steps: 
- Cumulus OK on dual 100Gb LAGs and jumbo frames — Karthik's plan for symmetric hashing + host bond mode sounds good.
- We can accept the rack token-bucket burst profile for the PoC (60Gbps / 12s) as a temporary testing threshold; for production we'll push for a higher negotiated cap in the SLA (we'll draft language).
- Equinox ordering is fine — Laura will drive procurement and crossconnect ordering. Laura, can you start the vendor request and loop in legal if needed?

Proposed PoC schedule:
- Nov 8: finalize crossconnect order with Equinox (if ordering today, ETA Nov 12).
- Nov 15–17: PoC deployment and soak (48 hours of mixed traffic including synthetic bursts).
- Nov 19: capacity readout and SLA negotiation kickoff.

Anita, can you confirm acceptance of the schedule and that netops will enable the requested LAG and burst policer during the PoC window?
